**suggestion (bug_risk):** Default `fontFamily` is skipped whenever `bodyStyle` is provided.

Using `style={bodyStyle ?? { fontFamily: DEFAULT_FONT_FAMILY }}` means any `bodyStyle` will drop the default `fontFamily`. If the intent is to keep the default font unless explicitly overridden, merge instead: `style={{ fontFamily: DEFAULT_FONT_FAMILY, ...bodyStyle }}`.

```suggestion
      <body
        className={bodyClassName}
        style={{ fontFamily: DEFAULT_FONT_FAMILY, ...bodyStyle }}
      >
```

1\. Ts exported as runtime 🐞 Bug ✓ Correctness 
@superfunctions/docs-theme points main/exports to TypeScript source files and has `noEmit:
true`, so it produces no JavaScript artifacts and will fail when imported at runtime (Node/most
bundlers can’t execute .ts/.tsx from dependencies by default). This makes the package unusable for
independent adoption/publishing as-is.
Agent Prompt ``` ### Issue description `@superfunctions/docs-theme` exports TypeScript source files (`./src/index.ts`) as its runtime entrypoints and is configured with `noEmit: true`, so there is no compiled JS output. This will break consumers at runtime. ### Issue Context Other workspace packages (e.g., `@superfunctions/http`) compile with `tsc` to `dist/` and export `dist/*.js` + `dist/*.d.ts`. ### Fix Focus Areas - packages/docs-theme/package.json[5-20] - packages/docs-theme/tsconfig.json[1-14] ### What to change - Add a `build` script (e.g., `tsc`) and configure `tsconfig.json` to emit JS + declarations to `dist/` (set `outDir`, `rootDir`, `declaration: true`, remove `noEmit`). - Update `main`, `types`, and `exports` to point to `./dist/index.js` and `./dist/index.d.ts`. - Ensure `tokens.css` is published at the exported path (either copy it into `dist/` during build and export `./dist/tokens.css`, or include the `src/tokens.css` file explicitly in `files` and export that path consistently). ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools

The `bodyStyle` nullish coalescing operator will skip the default font family if an empty object or any truthy value is passed. If `bodyStyle={{}}` is provided, no font family will be applied. Consider merging styles instead: ```tsx style={{ fontFamily: DEFAULT_FONT_FAMILY, ...bodyStyle }} ``` Or explicitly check for font family: ```tsx style={{ fontFamily: DEFAULT_FONT_FAMILY, ...bodyStyle }} ``` This ensures the default font is always set unless explicitly overridden by `bodyStyle.fontFamily`. ```suggestion ``` *Spotted by [Graphite](https://app.graphite.com/diamond/?org=21nCo&ref=ai-review-comment)*

**`branch` field required but never consumed** `DocsGitConfig` declares `branch` as a required field, but `createBaseLayoutOptions` only uses `user` and `repo` to build the `githubUrl`. Every caller must pass a `branch` value that is silently discarded, which is misleading API surface. Either make `branch` optional (if reserved for future edit-link generation), or use it in the URL — for example to link directly to the branch: ```suggestion export type DocsGitConfig = { user: string; repo: string; branch?: string; }; ```

**Default font silently dropped when `bodyStyle` is provided** `bodyStyle ?? { fontFamily: DEFAULT_FONT_FAMILY }` means that any non-nullish `bodyStyle` prop — even `{ background: '#fff' }` — will completely replace the font-family default. A consumer who passes `bodyStyle` for an unrelated reason (e.g. background color) will silently lose the brand font with no indication they need to add it manually. Consider spreading the default so the font stays unless explicitly overridden: ```suggestion ```

**`exports` point to raw `.ts` source — no build step** Both `"main"` and the `"exports"` `"default"` entry resolve to `.ts` source files instead of compiled output. This works within the monorepo because consumer apps (Next.js) transpile workspace packages themselves, but if the package is ever published to npm (it has no `"private": true`) external consumers without a TypeScript-aware bundler will receive un-compiled TypeScript and fail to import it. Consider either: - Adding `"private": true` to prevent accidental publishing, or - Adding a `build` script (e.g. `tsc -p tsconfig.json`) and pointing `exports` at `./dist`.

Consider either: - Adding `"private": true` to prevent accidental publishing, or - Adding a `build` script (e.g. `tsc -p tsconfig.json`) and pointing `exports` at `./dist`. How can I resolve this?
